To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the proposed methodology for establishing consistency of code and RFC documentation is feasible and can be applied in practice to a variety of network protocols; 2) the proposed symbolic implementation of the reduction scheme can be applied to protocols with a large number of internal transitions and is more efficient than the existing symbolic implementation of the refinement checker; and 3) the proposed methodology and the reduction scheme have been implemented in the tool ProVerif, which can be downloaded from our website.

(1) we have developed a methodology for verifying network protocols that is based on symbolic refinement checking, (2) we have implemented the methodology in the tool VerCors and have applied it to two case studies, and (3) we have developed and implemented a compression scheme that allows us to reduce the size of the models and thereby reduce the verification times.

(i) the problem of verifying network protocol implementations against RFC specifications can be formulated in terms of a refinement checking problem; (ii) the refinement checking problem can be simplified to a transition invariant checking problem; (iii) the simplification can be performed by automatic construction of witness module to deal with the specification state that is hidden in the implementation model; (iv) the simplification is useful for large case-studies; (v) the simplification reduces the problem to a verification problem for the specification
